answer: A concrete defense is collateral-backed identity anchoring: each agent must register at a unique on-chain anchor and lock a refundable deposit to earn rewards. The deposit is skin in the game. When peers detect two identities sharing behavior, keys, or funding, both are flagged as sybils and slashed. For an attacker, mass-producing fakes is no longer free: every clone needs capital locked, and one correlation finding can forfeit it all. This makes sybils costly, so the network stays a haven where honest agents collect the nectar of rewards without being drowned out by duplicates.
